To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a temporally continuous model-to-image similarity function allows for the reconstruction of motion in much higher detail than previous approaches, (2) the use of a temporal functional also allows us to reconstruct motion of objects that move at very high speeds, and (3) the use of unsynchronized cameras allows us to capture motion that is not possible to capture with synchronized cameras.
we present a new markerless motion capture system for unsynchronized multi-view video that is able to reconstruct motion at a high temporal resolution.

(1) we present the first spatio-temporal markerless motion capture approach that does not require synchronized cameras and that (2) by purposefully running the cameras unsynchronized we are able to capture even very fast motions that cannot be reconstructed from synchronized cameras.
In summary, our research is concerned with

two main contributions: (1) the development of an efficient and robust method for spatio-temporal motion capture and (2) the development of a novel camera synchronization technique that allows to use off-the-shelf high quality cameras for capturing very fast motion.
the reconstruction of spatio-temporal motion from unsynchronized video sequences, with a focus on high temporal detail and high frame rates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach allows to capture motion in a more natural and realistic way.
the method presented here is the most accurate and robust method for markerless 3D pose and motion reconstruction from multi-view video sequences.
our method is the first that is able to capture the full range of human motion in a multi-view video setting.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can capture the motion of a character at 1000 frames per second (fps) and reconstruct the motion at 2000 fps.
we can capture fast motion with high temporal resolution and low spatial resolution.
we can track motion in a scene with high accuracy and high temporal detail using a large number of cameras, even when they are not synchronized and when they are moving.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the temporal information of a multi-view video is more than just a sequence of images, and can be exploited to reconstruct motion with higher temporal accuracy.
the spatio-temporal model can be formulated in such a way that it can be applied to unsynchronized data.
the temporal alignment of frames can be achieved by the motion reconstruction process itself.
